subject: Initial: Sunrise Logistics portal access — SAML consent & metadata
messages:
From: Anna Liu <anna.liu@sunrise-ops.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: support@sunrise-ops.com
Date: 2028-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood portal invite & SAML metadata request

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the quick demo earlier — team is excited to move forward. We tried to accept the invite your team sent but ran into an error during the SAML handshake: after we upload our IdP metadata the portal responds with a 400 and a brief error about "missing EntityDescriptor/AssertionConsumerService".

Can you confirm what metadata format the Redwood portal expects? We attached our IdP export (idp-metadata-sunrise.xml) and a short checklist the procurement team asked us to complete. If there's a required field or an alternate endpoint we should use, please flag it.

Next steps from our side: procurement will need a PO template and estimated monthly token burn for our initial pilot.

Anna
IT Ops / Sunrise Logistics
Attachment: idp-metadata-sunrise.xml (xml)
Attachment: sunrise-procurement-questions.pdf (referenced)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Liu <anna.liu@sunrise-ops.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood portal invite & SAML metadata request

Hi Anna — thanks for the note and for attaching the metadata.

Quick diagnosis: our portal expects the EntityDescriptor element at the root and a single AssertionConsumerService (ACS) endpoint with binding="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-POST". A common issue is that some IdP exports include multiple ACS entries (e.g., sign-on and logout), and our import path currently picks the first ACS. If the first entry is a logout endpoint the import fails with that 400.

Ben — past hit on this? Can you share the internal checklist for SAML ingest?

Anna, to unblock you, can you either:
- send a trimmed metadata file with only the EntityDescriptor and a single ACS (POST) endpoint, or
- tell us which ACS in your file is the primary login URL and we'll patch the importer on our side (fast fix).

I've attached a short onboarding checklist (redwood_onboard-checklist.xlsx) with the PO template and our standard pilot token estimates. See the "SAML notes" tab for the exact XML fragment we parse.

Thanks,
Logan
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_onboard-checklist.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Anna Liu <anna.liu@sunrise-ops.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: support@sunrise-ops.com
Date: 2028-07-01T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood portal invite & SAML metadata request

Thanks Logan — we pulled a slimmed export and set the ACS to the POST endpoint only. Re-uploaded and now see a different behavior: the invite link still lands on the login page but after SSO it redirects to an error page that says "consent_required". The message is terse and there's no debug id.

Procurement attached the signed PO placeholder (will send final once SSO is green).

Could Marissa or Ben confirm if Redwood requires an explicit consent step (e.g., first-time app authorization) that our IdP must permit? If there's a URL pattern we can whitelist on our side to suppress a second consent, that would be great.

Anna
Attachment: sunrise-PO-placeholder.pdf (referenced)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Liu <anna.liu@sunrise-ops.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-02T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood portal invite & SAML metadata request

Hi Anna — short answer: yes, Redwood's private tenant flow can require an initial "app consent" step when a new org first authenticates via SAML, but that is configurable on the tenant. Right now your trial tenant is on the default path which shows a consent screen after successful SSO. We'll flip it off for your pilot tenant so users are taken directly to the dashboard after the assertion is accepted.

What we'll do for you by EOD today:
- Disable the post-SSO consent screen for your trial tenant (no changes required on your IdP).
- Add a small import tolerance so metadata with multiple ACS entries doesn't fail import (we'll prioritize the POST binding).
- Share the updated PO template and final pilot pricing in HubSpot and by DocuSign link.

Logan — can you confirm the DocuSign flow and send the HubSpot deal link to Anna? Marissa, tagging you for procurement approval on a one-off consent-off exception for DL-83921.

Regards,
Ben
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Onward: after Ben's change goes live, Anna should attempt a fresh invite acceptance and report whether the consent screen disappears. If anything still fails, we'll grab a transient debug id from the portal and escalate to platform infra.
